third-law.def: Newton's third law: when object A exerts a force on object B, B exerts a force on A that is equal in size, opposite in direction and of the same type. The two forces act on different objects, so they never cancel each other.

internal-force.def: A force that one part of a system exerts on another part. Internal forces come in third-law pairs that add to zero for the system.

external-force.def: A force exerted on a system by an object outside it. Only external forces can change how the system's center of mass moves.

ideal-string.def: A model string that has no mass and does not stretch, so the tension is the same all along it and the objects tied to it move together.

ideal-pulley.def: A model pulley with no mass and no friction. It changes the direction of an ideal string without changing its tension.
